# Runaway, and the distance to the break that does not couple in

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`runaway-distance-uncoupled` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F04 · [record](runaway-distance-uncoupled.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Every policy through the couplings, with the rest of the exchange fixed, that keeps its support leaves unused any larger stock coupled into it by threshold only; for such a stock, how far off the break is does not couple in before the break.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A formation g's policy goes through its couplings when, wherever the two flows have been alike through g's couplings up to a step, its take from and give to every condition coupled into g are alike in the two flows; the rest is fixed when every other formation's exchange on the conditions coupled into g is alike at every step; with the same formations present, the two give exchange following what couples in. (`Becoming.Flow.PolicyThrough`, `Becoming.Flow.OthersFixed`, `Becoming.Flow.ExchangeFollows`, `Becoming.Flow.exchangeFollows_of_policy`)
2. For every policy through the couplings with the rest fixed, the same formations present and balance at each step on what couples into g, the starts differing only in a stock coupled into g by threshold only, d higher in the second web: where the first web supports g at every step, the stock stands d higher and the webs are alike through g's couplings at every step. (`Becoming.Flow.policy_keeps_difference`, `Becoming.Flow.BalancesOn`, `Becoming.Web.CoupledInto`, `Becoming.Web.AlikeThrough`)
3. Under the same policy, rest, presence and balance, where the second web starts at least as high on what couples into g and alike on what couples into g by level, and a difference on a condition coupled into g has changed by a step, the first web did not support g at every earlier step. (`Becoming.Flow.policy_uses_after_failure`)
4. The web with stock c raised by d at every step, all else as it is, stands at least as high, supports whatever the web supports and stands alike elsewhere; it is dependent where the web is, and a flow balancing on a family balances there on it. (`Becoming.Web.raise`, `Becoming.Web.le_raise`, `Becoming.Web.Supported`, `Becoming.Web.Supported.raise`, `Becoming.Web.raise_other`, `Becoming.Web.Dependent`, `Becoming.Web.Dependent.raise`, `Becoming.Flow.BalancesOn.raise`)
5. At every step at which the web supports g, the web with a stock coupled into g by threshold only raised is alike through g's couplings; with the stock coupled in by level, every positive raise shows at every step. (`Becoming.Web.alikeThrough_raise`, `Becoming.Web.observed_raise_couples`)
6. Where c couples into g by threshold only and c is the only requirement of g that may be unmet up to a horizon u, some raise of c (in the proof, by the sum of the needs up to u) is alike through g's couplings at every step at which the web supports g and supports g at every step up to u: before the break, how far off it is does not couple in. (`Becoming.Web.needUpTo`, `Becoming.Web.need_le_needUpTo`, `Becoming.Web.break_not_bounded`)
7. In SupportDrawn the lower web fails the formation at the third step, and a raise is alike through its couplings at every step at which the lower web supports it, supports it at the third step and keeps the flow balanced. (`Becoming.SupportDrawn.break_uncoupled`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Balance is assumed only on the conditions coupled in, at each step (Flow.BalancesOn); the policy going through the couplings and the rest being fixed are supplied hypotheses, from which exchange following what couples in is derived; what others respond to is supplied.
- break_not_bounded further assumes that g does not observe c and that c is the only requirement that may be unmet up to the horizon, a local condition.
- Discrete steps, counted from step 0; natural-number levels, needs and amounts; decidable equality of conditions and formations is used only to split cases.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The laws do not derive that a formation draws more than is renewed, wants to keep its support or forms a policy.
- Loops and gain are not defined, so a runaway remains a reading; what is given here are the two theorems it rests on.
- The raised world uses the same flow, which after the break need not be what the formation would do.
- Near-definitional: the raised world is alike through the couplings because the stock is not among what couples in by level.
- Holds because the stock is unobserved by hypothesis; where it is observed, a break can often be seen coming, as early-warning signals of critical transitions show (Scheffer et al., Nature 2009).
- **Counterexample:** The rest being fixed is needed: where others respond to the stock itself, a higher stock can end the formation first (Attracting.higher_breaks_first), and T5 over policies fails. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Testing.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Ren's “wisdoms to avoid run away feedbacks”; testing-within-registration read a runaway as a loop running inside a blindness and marked it a heuristic; after experiment-needs-return the AI proposed stating it at the level of policies, and Ren answered “no extra review needed, merge, then continue”. Readings (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): a runaway is a loop through whose own couplings, before the break, the world is alike with a world with as much more stock as one likes; its policy cannot use a margin coupled into it by threshold only; avoiding it without forgoing what is there needs measurement, a model (理) or another formation's couplings; this reads Ren's words of 4 October that reason must regulate the heart so that its positive feedback loop does not run out of control.

  - Output: What couples in.

  - Preserved conditions: None. [Testing.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Testing.lean)
- **formal-reuse**: [laws-of-one-step](laws-of-one-step.md). Reuses Flow.BalancesOn: balance is assumed only on the conditions coupled in, and raising keeps it.
  - Output: Balance on a family across one step.
  - Input: The raised world still balances.
  - Preserved conditions: None. [Flow.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Flow.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [reserve-defers-ending](reserve-defers-ending.md). There a reserve defers the end and does not escape it; here how long it defers it does not couple in.
- related, not a proved adapter: [experiment-needs-return](experiment-needs-return.md). Knowing what one's own act does needs a return and a model of what is irrelevant; here coupling through support does not even give the distance to the break.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-a-carried-difference-grows](how-a-carried-difference-grows.md). Answers the item of its next step asking to define a loop in general and state a runaway as a theorem, for laws of exchange with given coupling strengths: a loop is a chain of couplings of positive strength back to where it started, and what reaches it is multiplied every time around by at least one plus the product of its strengths (carried_runaway); what runs away is the most difference that can arrive, attained by the carrying law. The runaway here is a policy keeping support, and connecting the two stays a next step.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-loops-form](how-loops-form.md). Here a runaway's break does not couple in before it; there the formation of the loop that runs away does not show in the amounts it carries either: what carries it is what the couplings themselves couple into.
- related, not a proved adapter: [loops-within-what-a-law-reads](loops-within-what-a-law-reads.md). Within one law: loops lie within what is read and form where reading grows; for a law reading a stock only below a threshold there is no loop through the stock before the break, and the loop forms at the break.
- related, not a proved adapter: [observation-is-a-route](observation-is-a-route.md). Observation is a route of readings from what is observed: a difference goes only downstream, and a stock couples into a formation only through a level it reads downstream of the stock; a route forms by closing.
